messages:
michael: Heads up — tens of pods in eu-west1 are returning connection_reset / 502 on outbound calls to model-registry.s3-like. Started ~09:12 UTC, correlates with a node rotation batch. Anyone else seeing this?

sre-bot: Alert: outbound_connection_fail_rate > 15% for cluster=eu-west1-edge (09:14)

anna: I’m seeing retries spike and Envoy logs show upstream premature close + TLS handshake failures. Not all pods, seems to hit ones on the rotated nodes first.

raj: Copying a snippet from envoy logs: `level=warning upstream reset reason=connection failure, reset_type=connection_failure, upstream_status=0, bytes_sent=0`

lina: Could be SNAT port exhaustion on the node NAT IPs after rotation — ephemeral ports getting reused. conntrack shows a lot of CLOSE_WAIT sockets around the same time.

paul: Quick check: `kubectl exec -n infra-net gateway-0 -- ss -s` shows TX queues high and many TIME_WAIT. Also seeing `tcp_reset` counts jump on the nodes that drained earlier.

michael: We route outbound via an egress-gateway with per-route cluster settings in Envoy. If gateway is hitting max connections, Envoy will start sending RSTs back. Were there any recent per-route ratelimit or max_conn changes?

raj: We did a config change last week to reduce `max_connections` on the egress cluster for model pulls to limit load. Config excerpt: ```yaml
clusters:
  - name: external-models
    connect_timeout: 1s
    lb_policy: ROUND_ROBIN
    common_http_protocol_options:
      idle_timeout: 1s
    max_requests_per_connection: 64
    max_connections: 200
```

anna: Hmm `max_requests_per_connection` + low `idle_timeout` + SNAT port churn could interact badly. If many short lived connections are being forced to re-open, we might blow ephemeral ports and then soak Envoy connections.

lina: On the nodes affected, `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` is default low (262144). The NAT IPs assigned to the rotated nodes changed; AWS NAT gateways show elevated metrics for ActiveConnections.

paul: Proposal: temporarily increase `max_connections` on external-models cluster and bump `idle_timeout` to 10s to allow connection reuse. Also raise node conntrack/nat timeouts to reduce TIME_WAIT pressure.

devops: I can push a canary bump to the Envoy config on 10% of egress gateways in eu-west1 now (will target {gateway-0..2}). Rolling it in 5m windows.

michael: Sounds good. Also add a temporary route to fallback to direct egress (bypass gateway) for traffic to model-registry.s3-like while we validate — reduces concentrated load on gateway.

raj: Deploy plan: (1) canary Envoy config changes: `max_connections: 600`, `idle_timeout: 10s`, `max_requests_per_connection: 0` (2) node sysctl bump `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30`, `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` (3) monitor active ephemeral port usage and 502 rate.

anna: I’ll watch the app-level retries and token costs — we might see transient duplicate pulls. Set alerts for >5% 502s and >2000 NAT active connections.

devops: Canaries started at 09:28. Patch id: cfg-2026-448. Rolling to 30% now.

sre-bot: Automated check: eu-west1 canary gateways healthy (09:31). Outbound error rate dropped from 18% to 3% on canary nodes.

michael: Good signal. Start rolling to 100% over the next 20m. Lina coordinate with infra to apply sysctl changes to the rotated node pool.

lina: On it — applying sysctl to nodes in batch. Will coordinate draining to avoid double rotations.

paul: After roll complete, follow-up: revisit per-route rate limits and consider connection pooling at the application layer for model pulls. We should also add an egress health-check that probes upstream availability pre-rotation to avoid concentrated reconnection storms.

anna: Note for postmortem — root cause likely config + node rotation timing exposing ephemeral port reuse and a tightened `max_connections` on the gateway.

michael: Thanks everyone. If any regressions ping me. :thumbsup:
